title: DAB-DETR: Dynamic Anchor Boxes are Better Queries for DETR
grouping: One tall dashed rounded container with a light-grey fill holds a single decoder layer, marked 'Nx' at its right edge; inputs (Spatial Positional Encodings, Decoder Embeddings, Anchor Boxes, Image Spatial Features) sit outside it at the bottom and left, the outputs leave through its top edge. A small legend at bottom right states the shape code.
shapes_depth: Two shape kinds, stated in the legend: square-cornered boxes are variables, rounded boxes are modules. Attention modules are orange rounded boxes, Add & Norm pale-yellow, FFN and MLPs light blue; variables are pink (Decoder Embeddings, Output), lavender (Anchor Boxes, Anchor Sine Encodings, New Anchor boxes) and grey (image features, positional encodings). Small circles mark operations: plus, C (concatenation), dot (element-wise product) and a sine glyph for the positional encodings. Wires are thin black orthogonal lines that hop over each other with small arcs; math labels such as (x, y, w, h), (w_ref, h_ref), (1/w, 1/h) and (dx, dy, dw, dh) ride on the wires.
proposed_highlight: The anchor box is the state being refined, and it keeps one colour (lavender) from the input Anchor Boxes through the sine encodings to New Anchor boxes at the top; the modified attention is named in full on its box (Width & Height-Modulated Multi-Head Cross-Attention).
lesson: Separate variables from modules by corner shape (square vs rounded, stated in a two-entry legend) and keep the refined state - here the anchor box - in one colour from input to updated output so its path through the layer can be traced.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2022'). The caption calls it the framework, but the drawing is the inside of one repeated decoder layer, so it is recorded as module-detail.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: training not depicted; DETR-style Hungarian matching.

core.what: one decoder layer drawn as a bottom-to-top stack (self-attention, add & norm, modulated cross-attention, add & norm, FFN, add & norm, output) inside a dashed frame marked Nx

relations.form: the decoder layer's blocks stacked bottom to top in a single column on the left of the dashed frame, with residual lines looping round each attention and FFN block
anchor-derived signals from the right enter the attention blocks' Q inputs through small concat (C) and multiply nodes, with (x,y) and (1/w,1/h) written on the incoming lines
the dashed Nx frame marks the layer as repeated, and an MLP at the top produces (Δx,Δy,Δw,Δh) into a 'New Anchor boxes' block that leaves the frame upward
a second, anchor-box stream runs up the right side of the frame (Anchor Boxes -> Anchor Sine Encodings -> MLPs) parallel to the decoder column

channels.colour: fills by block type: orange = attention, light blue = MLP/FFN, yellow-green = add & norm, pink = decoder embeddings and the output, lavender = anchor boxes, grey = image features and positional encodings
channels.shape: rounded box = module, square-cornered box = variable (keyed bottom right); small circles = concat, multiply, add and sine-encoding operators
channels.line: all solid black arrows; hop-over bumps mark crossings
channels.frame: one dashed rounded frame = the repeated decoder layer (Nx); inputs sit outside it

quality.strengths: The proposed width & height-modulated cross-attention is named in full in the largest orange block, and the anchor update is drawn as a separate right-hand path ending in 'New Anchor boxes', so where anchors enter and leave the layer is locatable.
quality.weaknesses: The routing into Q and K around the two concat nodes has many crossings with hop-over bumps and lines bending round blocks (image features and positional encoding wires snake under the stack); the module-vs-variable key relies on rectangle vs rounded corners, which barely differ; colour mixes role (input kinds) and block type; signal formulas are written on wires instead of as drawn representations.

insights.structure: One large dashed rounded frame marked 'Nx' holding one decoder layer as a bottom-to-top stack (self-attention, add & norm, modulated cross-attention, add & norm, FFN, add & norm, output), with an anchor-box branch (sine encodings, MLPs, New Anchor boxes) on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are coloured boxes outside the frame: grey Image Spatial Features and Spatial Positional Encodings on the left, pink Decoder Embeddings and lavender Anchor Boxes (x,y,w,h) at the bottom; tuple math labels the anchor lines.
insights.emphasis: Orange rounded boxes mark the attention modules, with the proposed 'Width & Height-Modulated Multi-Head Cross-Attention' named in full; the anchor update (Δx,Δy,Δw,Δh) loops to 'New Anchor boxes' at the top.
insights.flow: Bottom to top; the anchor path runs up the right side and feeds back across into Q via concat (C) and multiply (dot) nodes; V/K/Q labels sit at attention inputs.
insights.avoid: Many lines cross with small hop-over bumps near the concat nodes, making the Q/K routing hard to trace; the legend at bottom right uses shape (rectangle vs pill) that is not visually distinct enough.

arrangement.units: one dashed rounded frame for the repeated layer (Nx), inputs outside it
arrangement.inputs_as: coloured labelled boxes outside the frame at bottom and left (features, embeddings, anchor boxes)
